note.title: Digestive system and absorption
note.overview: Mechanical and chemical digestion produce small soluble molecules; most absorption occurs through the adapted wall of the small intestine.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 vocabulary for digestive system and absorption.
Apply the knowledge rather than relying on recognition alone.
Use the command word and include every required scientific point.
mustMemoriseRules: Oesophagus moves food by peristalsis; stomach churns and begins protein digestion; liver makes bile; gall bladder stores bile; pancreas makes digestive enzymes.
Small intestine completes digestion and absorbs soluble products; large intestine absorbs water.
Villi and microvilli increase area, thin walls shorten diffusion distance, and a good blood supply maintains gradients.

churns food, provides acidic conditions, kills many microbes and begins protein digestion

produces digestive enzymes that enter the small intestine
completes digestion and absorbs soluble digestion products into the blood
the opening through which faeces leave the body
movement of digested soluble molecules through the small-intestine wall into the blood
finger-like structures that greatly increase the surface area of the small intestine
wave-like muscular contractions that push food through the gut
